spec.description: New York's drinking water on its way through the mains, from DEP's sampling stations since 2015: the free chlorine that gives tap water its taste, how warm water uses it up every summer, and where it runs low. A timeline plays the seasons; a temperature brush, the boroughs and a drawn area filter the map and figures.

options.content:
### About the data

- **Samples**: NYC DEP, [Distribution Water Quality](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Environment/Distribution-Water-Quality/bkwf-xfky)
  (NYC Open Data), from 2015, when free chlorine starts under its present name, to the latest month DEP has published.
  Only samples from the distribution system (the mains), not the plants or the aqueducts.
- **Stations**: DEP names them only by a description ("N/S Lafayette Ave 1st SS W/O Underhill Ave"). Each is placed where
  its two streets meet on NYC's [street centerline](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/Centerline/inkn-q76z), or at its
  address on [NYC GeoSearch](https://geosearch.planninglabs.nyc), within some tens of metres; 16 of 372 could not be placed and
  are left off the map, though their samples count.
- **Almost none left** means under 0.2 mg/L of free chlorine, the least New York State asks for where water enters the mains;
  on the mains it asks only for a trace.

Built by `datasets/nyc-tap-water/build.sh` in pacha-dashboards (stations by `locate.py`). Times are New York's.

spec.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE coliform > 0) AS "Samples" FROM $samples WHERE $__crossfilter($waterFilters)

spec.rawSql:
-- Each sampling station in what the filters keep (the area drawn on this map left out, so every station stays):
-- its median free chlorine, the share of its samples with almost none left (under 0.2 mg/L), its median water
-- temperature, and its samples with coliform bacteria. The filters name bare columns: they go on $samples alone.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT site, round(median(chlorine), 2) AS chlorine, round(100.0 * avg(low), 1) AS low_pct,
         round(median(temperature), 1) AS temperature, count(*)::INTEGER AS samples,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE coliform > 0)::INTEGER AS coliform
  FROM $samples WHERE $__crossfilter($waterFilters, -area) GROUP BY site
)
SELECT st.site, st.borough, st.description, st.latitude, st.longitude, w.chlorine,
       -- the colour: 0.1 to 0.9 mg/L in six steps, a few stations above or below kept at the ends
       greatest(0.1, least(w.chlorine, 0.9)) AS colour, w.low_pct, w.temperature, w.samples, w.coliform
FROM w JOIN $stations st USING (site)
WHERE st.latitude IS NOT NULL

Draw an area to keep its stations.

options.content:
### What New York's tap water tastes of

Chlorine. DEP adds it where the water leaves the reservoirs, so that no germ survives the trip, and it is spent on the way:
by the time the water reaches a far end of the mains, there may be little left.

Some 390 **sampling stations** on the streets are the city's taste buds. DEP opens them a few times a month and measures
the free chlorine, the temperature, the turbidity and the bacteria. Where the aqueducts' water enters the mains, at the
tunnel shafts, it carries 0.75 mg/L; at the stations, 0.55 on the median.

**Summer** is when the chlorine runs out. Warm water uses it up faster: in July 2025 one sample in ten had less than
0.2 mg/L, against fewer than one in a hundred in December. Press play on the timeline and watch the dots turn red
every summer, or drag across the warm temperatures in the chart below.

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: every sample DEP took at a sampling station on New York's water mains since 2015, with the
-- station's place (none for the few unplaced, or no longer sampled): free chlorine (mg/L), water temperature (°C), turbidity (NTU), total coliform and E. coli
-- (MPN per 100 mL, 0 where none was found), the month of the year (m) and whether the chlorine was almost gone
-- (low: under 0.2 mg/L). From NYC Open Data's Distribution Water Quality (datasets/nyc-tap-water).
SELECT s.site, s.time AS t, s.chlorine, s.temperature, s.turbidity, s.coliform, s.ecoli,
       month(s.time)::INTEGER AS m, (s.chlorine < 0.2)::INTEGER AS low,
       coalesce(s.borough, st.borough) AS borough, st.latitude, st.longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/nyc-tap-water/samples.parquet') s
LEFT JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/nyc-tap-water/stations.parquet') st USING (site)
WHERE s.chlorine IS NOT NULL

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: DEP's sampling stations on the city's mains, placed where the two streets of their description
-- meet (or at their address), with how many samples each has and when they start and end.
SELECT site, borough, description, latitude, longitude, located, samples, first_sample, last_sample
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/nyc-tap-water/stations.parquet')
